front: Why is time-series data not i.i.d.?
back: Observations depend on their neighbours (not independent) and the distribution can drift (not identically distributed).
$y_t=T_t+S_t+R_t$: trend, seasonal component, residual. Use logs when seasonal swings grow with the level (multiplicative).

front: How do you remove a trend / a seasonal pattern?
back: First difference $y_t-y_{t-1}$ for a trend; seasonal difference $y_t-y_{t-m}$ for period $m$.
About $\pm 2/\sqrt n$; values outside suggest real autocorrelation.

Forecast one step, append it to the history as if observed, repeat. Errors compound; forecasts drift to the mean.
For each test time $t$: fit on data before $t$ only, predict $t$, advance. Expanding or sliding window; never shuffle.

front: Shape of the AR design matrix
back: $(n-p)\times(p+1)$: the first $p$ points lack a full history, plus one column of ones for the intercept.

front: Why does slow ACF decay worry you?
back: It often signals a trend / non-stationarity; difference the series before fitting a stationary model.
